sentences.en: Today, we are going to talk about anxiety, but not in the usual way that we normally talk about anxiety or not in the usual way that anxiety is spoken about.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们要谈谈焦虑，但不是以我们通常谈论焦虑的方式，也不是以通常人们谈论焦虑的方式。

sentences.en: Generally, we are going to do instead a complete and in-depth look into the neuroscience behind why anxiety happens, why it lingers, why it continues to be this like frustrating,
sentences.zh: 相反，我们将全面深入地研究焦虑产生的神经科学原理，为什么它会挥之不去，为什么它会持续成为生活中这种令人沮丧的、

sentences.en: sometimes like uncontrollable part of life.
sentences.zh: 有时甚至是无法控制的一部分。

sentences.en: I think knowing the intricacies behind anxiety and understanding the neuroscience behind the reactions that are going on in our brain is honestly sometimes the most important step
sentences.zh: 我认为了解焦虑背后的复杂性，理解大脑中正在发生的反应的神经科学原理，坦率地说，有时是变得不那么焦虑的最重要的一步，

sentences.en: in becoming less anxious because you start to like distance yourself from the feelings, you start to remove personal blame, you start to understand the systems better,
sentences.zh: 因为你开始与这些感觉拉开距离，你开始消除个人的自责，你开始更好地理解这些系统，

sentences.en: and you are able to apply logic and this information to your feelings that I think counteracts the,
sentences.zh: 并且你能够将逻辑和这些信息应用到你的感受中，我认为这抵消了，

sentences.en: I don't know, counteracts the illogical nature of anxiety.
sentences.zh: 我不知道，抵消了焦虑那种不合逻辑的本质。

sentences.en: That's what's been really helpful for me and I think just being able to explain what I'm feeling, how I'm feeling, why I'm feeling, whatever I am, puts this distance
sentences.zh: 这就是对我非常有帮助的地方，我认为仅仅能够解释我的感受、我的方式、我为什么会有这种感觉，无论是什么，都能在我与我的焦虑之间建立起这种距离。

sentences.en: between me and my anxiety.
sentences.zh: 在我与我的焦虑之间。

sentences.en: So that's what we're going to do today from talking about the function of different brain areas to neurotransmitters, cell networks, the neuroscience of fear.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我们今天要做的，从讨论大脑不同区域的功能到神经递质、细胞网络，再到恐惧的神经科学。

sentences.en: There is a lot to cover that is honestly, well, as a little bit of a psychology nerd, you guys know this, I find it so fascinating, not typically spoken about.
sentences.zh: 有很多内容要讲，老实说，作为一个心理学书呆子，你们都知道，我觉得这太迷人了，而且通常不会被谈论。

sentences.en: So without further ado, let's get into the neuroscience behind your anxiety.
sentences.zh: 所以废话不多说，让我们进入你焦虑背后的神经科学。

sentences.en: Firstly, why does anxiety feel so serious even if we rationally know, even if we consciously know, like the world isn't ending, like I'm going to be okay,
sentences.zh: 首先，为什么焦虑感觉如此严重，即使我们理性地知道，即使我们有意识地知道，世界并没有终结，我会没事的，

sentences.en: this thing is actually not a threat.
sentences.zh: 这件事实际上并不是威胁。

sentences.en: Why does our brain still take it to the extreme?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们的大脑仍然把它推向极端？

sentences.en: Anxiety feels so serious because your brain is not built to be calm, it is not built to be fair,
sentences.zh: 焦虑感觉如此严重，是因为你的大脑不是为了冷静而构建的，它不是为了公平而构建的，

sentences.en: it's especially not interested in your sense of fulfillment at all, it doesn't care if you're happy, first and foremost, it is built to protect you.
sentences.zh: 它尤其对你的成就感一点也不感兴趣，它不在乎你是否快乐，首先，它是为了保护你而构建的。

sentences.en: It does not care if you feel fulfilled, it doesn't care if you feel okay, it cares that you're alive.
sentences.zh: 它不在乎你是否有成就感，它不在乎你是否感觉良好，它在乎的是你还活着。

sentences.en: The system, your brain system, the system behind your anxiety would rather overreact and protect you than underreact and have something terrible happen.
sentences.zh: 这个系统，你的大脑系统，你焦虑背后的系统，宁愿过度反应来保护你，也不愿反应不足而导致可怕的事情发生。

sentences.en: One of the most useful ways neuroscientists now explain this is through prediction, a prediction model of anxiety.
sentences.zh: 神经科学家现在解释这一点最有效的方法之一是通过预测，即焦虑的预测模型。

sentences.en: Our brain predicts more than it reacts.
sentences.zh: 我们的大脑预测多于反应。

sentences.en: So much of what your unconscious brain is doing throughout the day is essentially just like constantly,
sentences.zh: 你的无意识大脑在一天中所做的大部分事情，本质上就像是不断地、

sentences.en: constantly making predictions about what is likely to happen next.
sentences.zh: 不断地对接下来可能发生的事情做出预测。

sentences.en: It consumes a large part of our unconscious mind.
sentences.zh: 它消耗了我们无意识思维的很大一部分。

sentences.en: In anxiety or amongst people who have anxiety, those predictions become more tilted towards threat and uncertainty.
sentences.zh: 在焦虑症中，或者在患有焦虑症的人群中，这些预测会更多地倾向于威胁和不确定性。

sentences.en: Whereas with someone who doesn't have anxiety, those predictions are more realistic and they're easier to dismiss, which if you are somebody who is anxious
sentences.zh: 而对于没有焦虑症的人来说，这些预测更现实，也更容易被忽略，如果你是一个焦虑的人，

sentences.en: probably feels literally impossible.
sentences.zh: 这可能听起来简直是不可能的。

sentences.en: I don't think I've ever been able to dismiss an anxious thought in my life without observing it, interrogating it, overthinking it.
sentences.zh: 我不认为我这辈子能不通过观察、审视、过度思考就忽略掉一个焦虑的想法。

sentences.en: But this is what happens in the minds of people without anxiety.
sentences.zh: 但这就是没有焦虑症的人大脑中发生的事情。

sentences.en: They don't have the same what we call learnt uncertainty.
sentences.zh: 他们没有我们所谓的习得性不确定性。

sentences.en: This is something that a paper in 2022,
sentences.zh: 这是2022年的一篇论文中提到的，

sentences.en: I think it was published in 2022,
sentences.zh: 我想是2022年发表的，

sentences.en: if you have anxiety, your brain has become primed to look for all the things in a situation that you don't understand, all the things that you aren't certain of
sentences.zh: 如果你有焦虑症，你的大脑已经被预设为去寻找情况中所有你不理解的事情，所有你不确定的事情，

sentences.en: and fill in those gaps with whatever will be the worst case scenario so that you can prepare.
sentences.zh: 并用最坏的情况填补这些空白，以便你能做好准备。

sentences.en: This is why your anxiety can become so all-consuming because it is focused on ambiguity.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么你的焦虑会变得如此消耗一切，因为它专注于模糊性。

sentences.en: It is obsessed with uncertainty and the possibility of threat and that possibility is always going to be there.
sentences.zh: 它沉迷于不确定性和威胁的可能性，而这种可能性将永远存在。

sentences.en: It is a fact of life.
sentences.zh: 这是生活的事实。

sentences.en: That's part of being alive.
sentences.zh: 这是作为生命的一部分。

sentences.en: But our brain can't help but fixate on it.
sentences.zh: 但我们的大脑忍不住要盯着它看。

sentences.en: This helps explain why your brain becomes like obsessed with certain thoughts, sensations, or themes, or what-ifs.
sentences.zh: 这有助于解释为什么你的大脑会变得像沉迷于某些想法、感觉、主题或“如果……怎么办”一样。

sentences.en: The very things that it cannot solve or cannot know for certain are the things that it becomes most obsessed with.
sentences.zh: 那些它无法解决或无法确定的事情，正是它最沉迷的事情。

sentences.en: It is not because those things are objectively the most important part of reality.
sentences.zh: 并不是因为这些事情在客观上是现实中最重要的一部分。

sentences.en: It's not that they're more likely to happen.
sentences.zh: 并不是因为它们更有可能发生。

sentences.en: It's not that they're more common.
sentences.zh: 并不是因为它们更常见。

sentences.en: It is just this anxious fallacy that the more I worry, the more it must be true.
sentences.zh: 这只是这种焦虑的谬论：我越担心，它就一定越真实。

sentences.en: The truth is is it's just that your brain has assigned these hypotheticals as important to think about more because they are scary, more because they are
sentences.zh: 事实是，这只是因为你的大脑将这些假设分配为更重要的思考对象，因为它们很可怕，更多是因为它们是

sentences.en: things that you can fixate on because there are so many possibilities, less because they are likely to happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以盯着不放的事情，因为有太多的可能性，而不是因为它们很可能发生。

sentences.en: The other thing that this threat detection system is built to do is generalize based on past experiences.
sentences.zh: 这个威胁检测系统被构建的另一件事是基于过去的经验进行概括。

sentences.en: Being the machine that it is,
sentences.zh: 作为一台机器，

sentences.en: your brain is a machine, once you may have experienced one dangerous or distressing situation, it becomes easier for your brain to then assume that every situation
sentences.zh: 你的大脑是一台机器，一旦你经历过一次危险或痛苦的情况，你的大脑就更容易假设每一种情况

sentences.en: has the possibility of morphing into that worst-case scenario.
sentences.zh: 都有可能演变成那种最坏的情况。

sentences.en: This is what is often referred to as fear,
sentences.zh: 这就是通常所说的恐惧，

sentences.en: generalization.
sentences.zh: 泛化。

sentences.en: And it is why anxiety tends to grow and expand over time.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么焦虑往往会随着时间的推移而增长和扩大。

sentences.en: You know, you can have a panic attack in a supermarket once and then over time as your brain begins to expect this fear in more and more situations, now you start to dread
sentences.zh: 你知道，你可能在超市里有过一次恐慌发作，然后随着时间的推移，当你的大脑开始在越来越多的情况下预期这种恐惧时，现在你开始害怕

sentences.en: going into any supermarket, going into anywhere that's public, going anywhere where there are people around you.
sentences.zh: 进入任何超市，进入任何公共场所，去任何周围有人群的地方。

sentences.en: You know, one humiliating social moment can spread into anxiety around eye contact, public speaking, being perceived at all.
sentences.zh: 你知道，一次尴尬的社交时刻可能会蔓延成对眼神交流、公开演讲、被他人注视的焦虑。

sentences.en: One scary bodily sensation can generalize into the fear of exercise, fear around caffeine, heat, crowds, even excitement.
sentences.zh: 一种可怕的身体感觉可以泛化为对运动的恐惧，对咖啡因、高温、人群甚至兴奋的恐惧。

sentences.en: These, like, it sounds irrational, right, that that fear could spread so rapidly, but it's, it may be irrational, it's not random, it's fear generalization.
sentences.zh: 这些，听起来很不合理，对吧，这种恐惧竟然能如此迅速地蔓延，但这，它可能是不合理的，但它不是随机的，它是恐惧泛化。

sentences.en: Now, this is where anxiety gets really irritating because
sentences.zh: 现在，这就是焦虑变得非常令人恼火的地方，因为

sentences.en: it's, because it starts to reach all these like broader aspects of life that shouldn't be scary.
sentences.zh: 它开始触及所有这些生活中本不该令人恐惧的更广泛的方面。

sentences.en: Like, why do I have this reaction, the same reaction to getting a cup of coffee as I would being chased by a tiger?
sentences.zh: 比如，为什么我对喝一杯咖啡的反应，和我被老虎追赶时的反应是一样的？

sentences.en: Well, you know, from the outside, yes, ordering a coffee is trivial, but from the inside, these small moments encompass multiple anxiety inducing aspects and multiple
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，从外部看，是的，点咖啡是琐碎的，但从内部看，这些小瞬间包含了多个诱发焦虑的方面和多个

sentences.en: moments of ambiguity.
sentences.zh: 模糊的时刻。

sentences.en: It might involve being watched, speaking whilst you're feeling shaky, making a mistake, feeling trapped in the queue, noticing your heart rate, you know,
sentences.zh: 它可能涉及被注视、在感到颤抖时说话、犯错、感到被困在队列中、注意到你的心率，你知道，

sentences.en: worrying that you'll panic, that you'll blush, freeze, that people will judge you.
sentences.zh: 担心你会恐慌、脸红、僵住、人们会评判你。

sentences.en: To the conscious, rational part of you, it is just a quick interaction.
sentences.zh: 对于你清醒、理性的那一部分来说，这只是一个快速的互动。

sentences.en: You are just ordering a coffee.
sentences.zh: 你只是在点一杯咖啡。

sentences.en: But, really, the brain is not only, it's not just computing the objective event, it's computing the meaning behind the event and the meaning and the harm or the anxiety
sentences.zh: 但实际上，大脑不仅是在计算客观事件，它还在计算事件背后的意义，以及过去经验的意义、伤害或焦虑，

sentences.en: of past experiences and it's sending in the whole army.
sentences.zh: 它正在派遣整支军队。

sentences.en: It thinks that every situation could become the worst thing ever.
sentences.zh: 它认为每一种情况都可能变成最糟糕的事情。

sentences.en: When we feel this sense of anxiety, our bodies and minds react in a way that basically makes it
sentences.zh: 当我们感到这种焦虑时，我们的身体和思想会以一种基本上使它

sentences.en: as easy as possible to get away, to notice more, to be more alert, to stay on guard,
sentences.zh: 尽可能容易逃离、更容易注意到、更警觉、保持戒备、

sentences.en: to fight back.
sentences.zh: 进行反击的方式做出反应。

sentences.en: From the body's and the brain's point of view, this is useful.
sentences.zh: 从身体和大脑的角度来看，这是有用的。

sentences.en: Putting us into this activated state is useful because if something dangerous does happen out of this hypothetical situation we've created, it's best to be prepared.
